channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Employees Concerned Over Release of Overly Powerful AI Models
item.description: Employees at AI development firms OpenAI and Anthropic are reportedly concerned that upcoming AI models may be too powerful for safe deployment. Sources indicate a growing gap between advanced AI capabilities and human control, potentially slowing industry progress. The companies are struggling to ensure the safety of these advanced, unreleased systems.

item.title: Medical Tourism Surges in Uzbekistan, Attracting One in Four Tourists from Neighboring Countries
item.description: Medical tourism is becoming a primary reason for travel to Uzbekistan from neighboring states, with one in four surveyed tourists visiting for treatment. While visiting relatives was previously the main driver for 80% of regional visitors, it now accounts for 25.2%. Tourism for leisure, shopping, and business also contributes significantly.

item.title: Kazakhstan Establishes State Commission to Oversee Infrastructure Program Funds
item.description: A state commission has been formed in Kazakhstan to monitor the spending of funds allocated for the "People's Construction" infrastructure modernization program, set to be implemented by 2027. The commission, headed by the Chairman of the Supreme Audit Chamber, Alikhan Smailov, will include representatives from various government bodies, parliament deputies, and public figures to ensure transparent and effective use of budget funds.

item.title: Kazatomprom Shares Fall Over 4% Following Top Managers' Arrests
item.description: Kazatomprom's global depositary receipts (GDRs) on the London Stock Exchange dropped by over 4% in early trading, while shares on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange (KASE) fell by 3.5%. This decline follows news of the detention of a board member in a corruption case. The company's stock has been trending downwards since early November.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Official Urges Against Politicizing Nomination Support Process
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's presidential press secretary, Askat Alagözov, stated that citizens can support multiple presidential candidates through the "Tunduk" app until December 8th. He urged officials to provide correct information to employees regarding the nomination support process, warning that candidates unable to gather the required 30,000 signatures might politicize the situation and falsely accuse the authorities of obstruction.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Invites UK King Charles III and Prime Minister to Visit
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has invited King Charles III and UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak to visit Kyrgyzstan in 2027. The invitation was extended during a meeting with the new British Ambassador, Vicente Salles Ducar, who presented his credentials. Japarov highlighted strong bilateral relations and economic cooperation interests.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Receives New UK Ambassador
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov received the Ambassador of the United Kingdom and Northern Ireland, Vicente Solera Duecar, for the presentation of credentials. Japarov noted the strong foundation of mutual trust and respect in the 30-year diplomatic relationship and expressed satisfaction with its active development. He highlighted trade, economic, and investment cooperation, as well as educational and tourism ties.

item.title: Kazatomprom Issues Statement Following Omarbekov's Detention
item.description: Kazatomprom has released a statement following the detention of Omarbekov. The statement addresses the circumstances surrounding the event and provides the company's official position. Further details regarding the content of the statement are expected.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election: Official Urges Support for Candidates
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's presidential press secretary, Askat Alagozov, has urged government and municipal officials to inform their staff about supporting presidential candidates via the 'Tunduk' app. He reminded citizens that signatures can be submitted until December 8th, emphasizing that this is a legal requirement for candidate registration, not a vote. Alagozov cautioned against politicizing the process if candidates fail to gather the required 30,000 signatures.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Parliament Debates Development Initiatives: New Towns, Healthcare, and Infrastructure
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's parliament discussed several development initiatives, including granting district town status to Myrza-Ake and Kara-Kulja villages, gasifying Medrese village, and building a maternity and child care center. Deputies also raised concerns about school and kindergarten shortages, the need for school buses, and improving drinking water supply and transport infrastructure in various regions. Proposals also included completing school construction and upgrading power lines.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Full Ban on Energy Drink Production and Import
item.description: A Kazakh lawmaker has proposed a complete ban on the production and import of energy drinks, citing health concerns. The proposal follows recent incidents where young individuals suffered severe health issues linked to excessive consumption of these beverages. Stricter regulations are being considered.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Simplifies Business Registration to Five Minutes, Says Entrepreneur
item.description: The Kyrgyz government is strengthening support for entrepreneurs through simplified procedures and preferential loans, according to Nurdin uulu Nurtilek, director of LFC company. He stated that company registration can now be completed in just five minutes, with most documentation handled online.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans International School and Science Park Modeled on Russia's Sirius
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Russia's Sirius federal territory plan to establish an international school, a center for gifted children, and a youth science park. A joint working group will address financing, construction, and management. Discussions also included educational programs for Kyrgyz students and teachers, and a 'Kyrgyzstan-Sirius' Summit of Talents in Bishkek.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Investigators May Access Digital Data Without Court Sanction in Emergencies
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's investigators will be able to examine citizens' digital communications and personal data without prior court approval in exceptional circumstances. Amendments to the criminal procedure code, published November 24, allow for this in urgent cases where evidence might be lost. The investigator must notify a prosecutor and judge within 24 hours.

item.title: International Campaign Against Violence Launched in Bishkek
item.description: An international campaign, '16 Days of Activism Against Violence,' aimed at preventing domestic and gender-based violence, has begun in Bishkek. The event included discussions on preventing violence against women and girls, online harassment, and legal accountability. A march and social play were also organized.

item.title: Mayor of Kant Resigns Following Presidential Order
item.description: The Mayor of Kant city in the Chuy region, Ulan Mailibashev, has been dismissed from his post. The decision was made in accordance with Article 71 of the Constitution and Article 47 of the law on local state administrations and self-governing bodies, as per a decree signed by President Sadyr Japarov.

item.title: Proposal for Higher Water Tariffs for Some Car Washes in Kazakhstan
item.description: A proposal has been made in Kazakhstan to introduce higher water tariffs for certain car washes. Deputy Sergey Ponomarev highlighted the country's water scarcity, projecting a deficit of 15 billion cubic meters by 2040. He noted that 85% of registered car washes operate without water recycling systems, consuming up to 250 liters of drinking water per wash.

item.title: Uzbekistan and France Expand Cooperation in Technical Regulation and Product Safety
item.description: Uzbekistan and France are strengthening cooperation in technical regulation, conformity assessment, and product safety. Anvarjon Zokirov, Director of the Uzbek Agency for Technical Regulation, met with French Ambassador Walid Fouque and representatives from Bureau Veritas. Two documents were signed between Bureau Veritas and the Uzbek Institute of Standards to enhance collaboration in consumer goods, electrical equipment, and textiles.

item.title: Tajikistan Approves Procedure for Anti-Discrimination Expertise of Legal Acts
item.description: The government of Tajikistan has approved a procedure for conducting anti-discrimination expertise of normative legal acts and their drafts. This step aims to strengthen legal guarantees of equality and prevent discrimination, aligning national legislation with international human rights standards. The approved procedure defines the mechanism for identifying and eliminating discriminatory norms.

item.title: Kazakh Tenge Weakens Against US Dollar, Experts Cite Market Factors
item.description: The Kazakh Tenge has weakened against the US dollar, with the exchange rate reaching 459.43 tenge per dollar. Financial analysts attribute this depreciation to natural market corrections and global oil market dynamics, rather than a catastrophic fall. Experts suggest the Tenge is returning to more familiar economic values.

item.title: Kazakhstan's KMG Expects Board of Directors Change Amid Samruk-Kazyna Corruption Case
item.description: Kazakhstan's national oil company, KazMunayGas (KMG), anticipates a change in its board of directors. This potential reshuffling comes in the wake of a corruption case involving the sovereign wealth fund Samruk-Kazyna. The details surrounding the expected board changes remain unspecified.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allows Minors to Donate Stem Cells to Siblings After Legal Change
item.description: Kazakhstan has passed a bill allowing minors to donate hematopoietic stem cells to their siblings. Previously, no specific procedure existed for underage donors. The new regulation requires genetic compatibility and consent from parents and the child, facilitating treatment for children with malignant blood diseases.

item.title: Kazakh MP Criticizes HR Enbek Platform for Creating Artificial Job Market
item.description: A Kazakh member of parliament has stated that businesses are forced to post fake job openings on the HR Enbek platform to avoid fines. This practice misleads job seekers and creates an artificial market, hindering real job searches. The MP also criticized requirements for advance notification of layoffs.

item.title: New Center and Electric Buses Planned for Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve
item.description: A new visitor center with amenities like restrooms, a coworking space, and a cafe is planned for Kyrgyzstan's Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve. Electric buses will transport tourists within the reserve, with asphalt roads also being laid. The project aims to improve tourist experience and manage access, with implementation expected in 2027.

item.title: Kazakh Businessmen Risk Losing Land and Investments Due to Delayed State Land Disputes
item.description: Kazakh businessmen face the risk of losing land and millions in investments as state bodies challenge their own decades-old land grants. The 'Ak Zhol' party faction demands time limits for disputing land allocations, arguing that officials' errors should not penalize entrepreneurs who have built on and paid taxes for these properties.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ratifies UN Convention Against Cybercrime
item.description: Kazakhstan's parliament has ratified the UN Convention Against Cybercrime, establishing a legal framework for international cooperation in combating digital offenses. The convention criminalizes various cybercrimes, including unauthorized access and data theft, and facilitates information exchange and joint investigations. A 24/7 network of contact points will be established to enhance collaboration.

item.title: IOM Builds 514 Shelters for Earthquake-Affected Families in Kunar Province, Afghanistan
item.description: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Afghanistan has constructed 514 shelters for families affected by an earthquake in Kunar Province. Supported by the European Union and the Netherlands, these homes will provide protection from the harsh winter conditions for residents of the Nurgl district.

item.title: Organizers of Buyers Union Financial Pyramid Sentenced in Astana
item.description: Five individuals have been found guilty of creating and managing the Buyers Union financial pyramid in Astana. Operating from June 2024 to February 2025, the scheme defrauded 44 people of over 111 million tenge by promising interest-free housing and car purchases. Sentences range from 5.5 to 7.5 years.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sets November 29 for Early Maslikhat Elections
item.description: Kazakhstan will hold early elections for maslikhat (local representative body) deputies on November 29. Citizens can find their polling station details online via government websites and the eGovMobile app. Election campaigning concludes on November 28. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev previously dissolved all maslikhats.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov Dismisses Four District Governors and Two City Mayors
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan has dismissed four district governors and two city mayors following a review of local government performance for the first nine months of 2026. The dismissals were made in accordance with the Constitution and relevant laws on local governance. Some officials had already been reported to be leaving their posts.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discusses AI-Driven Cyber Threats to Users, Businesses, and Children in 2026
item.description: Experts at Kaspersky's Cybersecurity Weekend in Tashkent discussed emerging AI-driven cyber threats for 2026. They highlighted the first AI-executed cyberattack and detailed risks to users, businesses, and children online. Statistics show 53.2% of users in Uzbekistan faced local threats from January to September 2026, including malware via flash drives and fake installers.

item.title: Taliban Economy Minister Seeks Lifting of Economic Sanctions from UN Representative
item.description: During a meeting with the head of UNAMA, the Taliban's Economy Minister requested the removal of economic sanctions. The specific details of the discussion and the UNAMA head's response were not provided in the source text.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Prison Deputy Head Sentenced to 11 Years for Aiding Inmate's Drug Trafficking
item.description: A deputy head of a prison in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, has been sentenced to 11 years in prison for facilitating an inmate's online drug trafficking operation. The official created conditions for the inmate to manage an internet store via phone, receiving material benefits in return.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways (KTZ) Postpones IPO to 2027 Amidst Global Market Concerns
item.description: Kazakhstan's national railway company, KTZ, has again postponed its initial public offering (IPO) to 2027, following advice from international investment banks due to a deteriorating global financial market. This decision follows previous delays and coincides with recent arrests of KTZ leadership on corruption charges.

item.title: Kazakhstan Preparing to Extradite Chechen Activist Mansur Movlayev to Russia, Rights Advocates Claim
item.description: Human rights advocates and lawyers claim Kazakhstan is preparing to extradite Chechen activist Mansur Movlayev, currently in extradition detention in Almaty, to Russia. Movlayev is known for his opposition to Russia's war in Ukraine. His lawyer has filed an appeal against the extradition decision.

item.title: Kazakhstan Employers Forced to Post Fake Job Vacancies, Says Deputy
item.description: Kazakh employers are compelled to post fictitious job vacancies, according to Kurultai deputy Arman Kozhahmetov. He stated that the HR Enbek platform imposes excessive, non-legislative requirements, forcing businesses to list vacancies even when a candidate is already chosen. This practice misleads job seekers and creates an artificial labor market.

item.title: Parliament Speaker Denies Motorcades Cause Bishkek Traffic Jams
item.description: Marlen Mamataliev, the speaker of Kyrgyzstan's parliament, refuted claims that state motorcades are the primary cause of traffic congestion in Bishkek. He attributed the jams to the city's railway crossings, which narrow traffic flow. Mamataliev suggested that opening more railway crossings could alleviate the problem.

item.title: Batken Mayor Dismissed Following President's Criticism
item.description: Seitek Kulubayev has been dismissed as the mayor of Batken, Kyrgyzstan, following President Sadyr Japarov's criticism of local authorities. The dismissal came after a meeting where Japarov highlighted shortcomings in regional governance and inefficient use of development funds. The official reason for Kulubayev's dismissal was not specified.

item.title: Kazakhstan Continues Arrests of Top Managers in Major Companies Amid Corruption Probe
item.description: Kazakhstan's anti-corruption service has detained and placed several top managers of major companies, including from Kazatomprom, in a temporary detention center. They are suspected of involvement in a corruption scheme organized by the former leadership of Samruk-Kazyna. Pre-trial investigation is underway.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Labor Ministry Denies Rumors of Social Benefit Cancellations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection has refuted claims circulating on social media about the cancellation or reduction of social benefits. The ministry stated that the government remains committed to its social obligations and is working to improve the fairness and targeting of social support systems.
